3.19_sampling_jitter.note: WindowScorer.append()/try_score() are driven purely by SAMPLE COUNT (a deque with maxlen + a new_samples counter), not by wall-clock timestamps -- they never see the real time between samples at all. So as long as samples keep arriving (no drops), +/-2ms, +/-5ms jitter, or delayed samples cannot change crash_prob/recon_error even in principle -- confirmed empirically: replaying the identical sample sequence twice produces bit-identical output regardless of any timing simulated around the calls. The real place jitter could matter is the caller's OWN real-time pacing loop (next_tick logic in crash_monitor.py main() / exp_a4's replay loop), which 3.1 above already measured directly (0 deadline misses over 15 real minutes).

3.20_dropped_sample_simulation.note: Both sparse (1-in-20) and burst (30 consecutive) sample drops run through WindowScorer with NO exception and NO detection/logging of the gap -- the deployed code has no drop counter or gap-detection logic at all. A dropped sample silently means the window it would have joined just has one fewer real distinct reading spread over more real elapsed time; the model scores whatever samples DID arrive as if they were perfectly regular. This is a real, worth-flagging gap for the paper's robustness discussion: sample loss is currently invisible to the running system.

3.27_causal_filter_state_reset.cold_start_note: CausalGravityFilter.apply()'s first-ever call initializes self.gravity = accel_xyz.copy(), so the very first output is always exactly [0,0,0] regardless of the true reading -- a known, real startup transient bias, not a bug, just worth stating explicitly.
3.27_causal_filter_state_reset.clear_note: WindowScorer.clear() (called in crash_monitor.py main() right after a 30s alarm countdown) only clears the sample buffer and new_samples counter -- it does NOT reset gravity_filter. So after every alarm-countdown gap, the causal gravity EMA resumes from its STALE pre-gap estimate rather than re-initializing fresh, and needs roughly a few EMA time constants (~1-2s at this filter's 0.3Hz cutoff) of new real samples to reconverge. Not necessarily wrong (arguably better than a fresh cold-start-zero transient right after a real crash event), but genuinely undocumented behavior worth stating for the paper.

3.28_startup_grace_period.note: try_score() returns None (TriggerPolicy.update() is never even called) until the buffer holds a full window_samples=60 readings AND a full stride_samples=15 have accumulated -- confirmed empirically: the first non-None result appears at exactly sample #60, matching config exactly. No partial window is ever scored, and no alert can fire before 1.2s (60 samples @ 50Hz) of continuous real sampling has occurred from a cold start or after any buffer clear.
